# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book collects the simulation studies and methods notes written while
developing the R package [easyRasch2](https://pgmj.github.io/easyRasch2/). Each
chapter starts from a question that came up when choosing a default, a cutoff or
a statistic for the package, and reports what the simulations showed. Most of
them will never become journal articles, but the results are useful beyond the
package, and they should be possible to find, check and cite.

## How the chapters work

Every chapter is self-contained and can be read on its own. Where one study
depends on another, the dependency is a cross-reference to that chapter.

Each chapter opens with a box giving its status, the easyRasch2 and R versions
it was computed with, and a suggested citation. The status is one of:

- **Complete.** The study answers its question and the results are not expected
  to change.
- **Preliminary.** The design is settled, but parts are still running or being
  checked.
- **Superseded.** A later chapter replaces it, and the box says which.

The dates under each chapter title are when it was first published and last
modified. A revision that changes a result is listed in the chapter's revision
history, with what changed and why. Edits to wording are not listed. The full
history of every chapter is in the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/pgmj/rasch_book), linked from the
"View source" button on each page.

## Reproducibility

The code that produces each table and figure is in the chapter, folded by
default. Simulations that take more than a few minutes do not run when the book
is built. They are in the `scripts/` folder of the repository, one subfolder per
topic, and the chapter says which script produced which result. Some chapters
call internal easyRasch2 functions with `easyRasch2:::`. These are not part of
the package's public interface and may change between versions.

## Citing

Cite a chapter as a chapter in this book, with its last revised date. Each
chapter's opening box gives the suggested citation.

## Feedback

Corrections and questions are welcome as
[GitHub issues](https://github.com/pgmj/rasch_book/issues). The "Report an
issue" button on each page opens one for that chapter.
